<translate>
<!--T:1-->
The page of an artwork (''Object details'') brings together everything the catalogue knows about one work. Not every work has every section: a section appears only when the catalogue has information for it.

<!--T:2-->
== At the top ==
* '''Images''' of the work. Click an image to enlarge it. For a suite, the page shows the images of the works in the suite.
* The '''artist''' and the work's '''Reference''': its number in the catalogue raisonné.
* The '''title''', the '''type of work''' (painting, print, sculpture and so on), the '''date''' and the '''place''' of creation. Dates can be approximate; words such as ''approximate'', ''before'' or ''after'' say how certain they are.
* For works in a '''suite''' (a series such as a portfolio of prints): the suite they belong to and their position in it. On the suite itself: the works it includes.
* The '''materials and techniques''', for example oil on canvas or etching on paper.

<!--T:3-->
== Description ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What it contains
|-
| '''Attributes''' || Signatures, dates, numbers, stamps and other marks on the work, with what they say and where they are, for example ''signed and dated, front bottom right''
|-
| '''Dimensions''' || The measurements, for example height × width × depth in cm, often several: for the image, the sheet or the frame. Qualifiers such as ''sight'' (measured within the frame) or ''approximate'' say how they were taken.
|-
| '''Parts of the object''' || For works made of several pieces, such as a triptych: each part with its own data
|-
| '''Editions''' || For prints and sculptures: the editions, such as the regular edition, artist's proofs or casts, with their number and numbering
|-
| '''Location''' || Where the work is today, where this may be published
|-
| '''Other Titles''' || Further titles of the work: translations, alternative titles, or titles used in particular publications or by particular owners
|-
| '''Notes''' || Further information from the catalogue's authors
|}

<!--T:4-->
== History ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What it contains
|-
| '''Agents''' || People and institutions involved in making the work: printer, publisher, foundry, collaborators
|-
| '''Dates''' || Dated events in the work's life: when it was finished, printed, signed, restored and so on
|-
| '''Exhibitions''' || The exhibitions where the work was shown
|-
| '''Provenance''' || The previous and present owners, with their periods of ownership, as far as they may be published
|-
| '''References''' || The publications in which the work is mentioned or illustrated, with page and illustration number
|-
| '''Related objects''' || Links to other works: studies, versions, copies, models and similar
|-
| '''Tags''' || The artist's keywords for the work; click one to see all works with it
|}

<!--T:5-->
Names of people, institutions, exhibitions and publications are usually links: they lead to the respective page, for example to everything the catalogue holds about a gallery. A small book icon after a value marks its sources: point at it to see their titles, or click or tap it to list them (see [[Sources and citations#Reading sources|Reading sources]]).

<!--T:6-->
== At the bottom ==
* '''Sources''', if the work has any: the number of its citations and those of the work as a whole, which say where the information on the work comes from (see [[Sources and citations#Reading sources|Reading sources]]).
* The '''copyright''' notice for the images.
* '''Share with others''': links to share the page.
* '''Contact the artist''': ways to contact the artist or the catalogue's authors, as far as they publish them. ''email through open.cr'' opens your own email program with a message to the artist's address at openCR. Use it to ask a question about the work or to share information, for example if you own the work or know of an exhibition that is missing.

<!--T:7-->
== Works for sale ==
If a work is for sale through a gallery, a dealer or the artist, the page shows the offer under '''Available for sale''': the seller (''Available from''), the condition, the price or ''Price on request'', and a short text. '''See the seller's page''' leads to the seller's own page about the offer; where there is none, '''Ask the seller''' opens a page that names the work and lists the seller's published contact details. An offer can also be for one edition or one part of the work; it is then labelled with that edition or part.

<!--T:8-->
Adverts for the artist's work in general appear under '''Works by this artist for sale''', on the artist's page and on the pages of the artist's works.
</translate>
